name: BSP_SceneProperty_CopyReferencePayload
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet cc2_property_bag_merge, read-only analysis. __thiscall(dword* destPayload /*ECX = record+18h*/, dword* sourcePayload), RET 4. Copies the two-dword reference payload: the tag at +18h verbatim and the target name at +1Ch as a fresh 00438E40 duplicate. The decompiler's early return after the free is wrong; the bytes at 008F0355 are 50 E8 2E663000 83C404 C746 04 00000000 (PUSH EAX / CALL free / ADD ESP,4 / MOV [ESI+4],0) falling through to the JZ target 008F0365, so it frees the old name, nulls it and then copies. It does NOT touch record+08h, so an assigned reference keeps the destination's kind. Caller: 008F0771, the type-5 arm of 008F0700.

name: BSP_SceneProperty_CopyArrayBlock
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet cc2_property_bag_merge, read-only analysis. __thiscall(dword* destBlock /*ECX = record+20h*/, dword* sourceBlock), RET 4. Frees the destination's old block, nulls it (008F03C4: ... 83C404 C706 00000000, then the JZ target 008F03D3), stores the source's byte size at +24h and deep-copies the data with operator new (008F03D7) and memcpy (008F03E1). The size is used as a BYTE count by both, which is what fixes record+24h as a byte size rather than an element count. One arm serves all four array codes 8..0Bh and there is no stride check. Caller: 008F07B6 in 008F0700.

name: BSP_SceneProperty_ReleaseArrayBlock

name: BSP_SceneProperty_SetReference
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. name: BSP_SceneProperty_ReleaseValue
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet cc2_property_bag_merge, read-only analysis. __fastcall(SceneProperty* /*ECX*/). The per-type release behind the record's single vtable slot: 004E6730 is the scalar deleting destructor stored at record+00h by every constructor, it forwards through the thunk 008F0DE0, and this routine switches on the type code at +04h. Type 2 frees +0Ch, type 5 frees +1Ch, type 6 calls the sub-bag's own deleting destructor with 1, types 8..0Bh call 008F03F0; the shared tail zeroes +04h, +08h, +0Ch and +28h. +28h is never freed, so the enum/LUA_S declaration object is shared and not owned. This is also the evidence that the twelve type codes are one class with a tag, not twelve subclasses: 008EF148, 008EF2B0, 008EF2F8 and 008F38A0 all store the same vtable 00CE89D4.

name: BSP_SceneProperty_AssignValueFrom

name: BSP_ScenePropertyBag_Find
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet cc2_scene_property_bag, read-only analysis. __thiscall(ScenePropertyBag* /*ECX*/, const char* key), RET 4. Splits the key at the first '.' (_strchr at 008F228A); with no dot it builds a native string and calls the map find 0043B8B0 on this+4, returning *(node+8) (the 38h property record) or 0. With a dot it copies the head into the shared global buffer 00F89658 (so the routine is not reentrant), looks that up, and recurses on the tail at 008F232B with ECX = record+0Ch only when *(record+4) == 6, which is what makes type 6 the nested sub-bag. name: BSP_SceneProperty_SetValueFromToken

name: BSP_ScenePropertyBag_Insert
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet cc2_scene_property_bag, read-only analysis. __thiscall(ScenePropertyBag* /*ECX*/, const char* key, SceneProperty* record), RET 8, returns the bag. name: BSP_ScenePropertyBag_SetString

name: BSP_ScenePropertyBag_Parse
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet cc_scene_records, read-only analysis; already described as the property-bag parser by docs/SCENE_FILE_READER.md. __fastcall(Tokenizer* /*ECX*/, char allowUntypedValues, int parseGroupList). Optional '( name name ... )' group list, then '{'; the body loop reads a key, looks it up with 008f2260, and if the next token is '=' consumes it and runs the per-type read for the letter, otherwise recurses into a sub-bag only when the next token is '{' and silently drops the key when it is neither (008f6xxx else branch). Every typed read ends with BSP_SceneTokenizer_ExpectToken 008d9930 for the ';', which peeks and consumes only on a match, so a property authored without its terminator costs one reported error and consumes nothing further. That bounded read is what the reconstruction's value scan had to be corrected to; see docs/SCENE_FILE_READER.md Corrections. | CORRECTION, packet cc2_scene_property_bag: the ABI above is wrong. RET 0Ch is three stack arguments and ECX is the BAG, not the tokenizer: 008F5A25 copies ECX into EBX and spills it to [ESP+18h], from where it is reloaded as the this of every 008F3xxx setter (008F5D17, 008F6724) and of the recursive call at 008F6740, while 008F5A1E loads the tokenizer from the first stack argument into ESI for every 008D8xxx/008D9xxx call. So __thiscall(ScenePropertyBag* /*ECX*/, Tokenizer*, char allowUntypedNumbers, void* groupRegistry). Argument 3 is not a boolean: 008F5A47 loads it into EDI and 008F5AA9 calls 00469B60 on it to turn each name of the leading '( name name ... )' list into a bag, which 008F5AB3 then merges with keepExisting = 0, so that list is inheritance and a group's values overwrite. Argument 2 is the byte at [ESP+154h] that forces the I and F readers to read even when 008D8F10/008D8F40 say the next token is not a number. The twelve type codes, their letters, the eight reference sub-kinds and the 114h bag layout are in docs/SCENE_PROPERTY_BAG.md.
